name: Applebeez Neighborhood Feeding Trough
tagline: EATIN' GOOD IN THE PARKING LOT
address: 4400 Outlot Parkway, Pad Site C, Behind The Former Bank, Sterling Commons
about: Applebeez Neighborhood Feeding Trough is a neighborhood bar and grill serving a neighborhood that is legally a parking lot. Our dining rooms are decorated with authentic antiques purchased in bulk from a single vendor. Riblets are available.
announcement: RIBLETS ARE AVAILABLE. RIBLETS HAVE ALWAYS BEEN AVAILABLE.

promos.text: Buy 1, Get 1 Half (Half is a size)

reviews.name: Dwayne H.
reviews.text: Ordered the riblets. Received riblets. The system works.

reviews.name: Marguerite O.
reviews.text: The bowl did not fit in my refrigerator, so I ate all of it. No complaints filed.

reviews.name: Kelsi R.
reviews.text: Declined the 2 For $22 and was charged for the 2 For $22. Staff explained this clearly and at length. Four stars for the explanation, two for the meal.

reviews.name: Ronald P.
reviews.text: I have retained eleven souvenir vessels. My cabinets are full. I will be returning Thursday.

reviews.name: Anette V.
reviews.text: The televisions were all showing the same frozen frame of a football game. I found this restful.

menu.name: The Sampler Wall
menu.blurb: Platters engineered for a table that will not agree on anything.

items.name: Neighborhood Overflow Sampler
items.desc: Four appetizers arranged on one platter until the platter is no longer visible. Sharing is assumed and is not enforced.
items.imagePrompt: Ultra-premium commercial food photography for a delivery-app menu tile. Subject: an enormous oval platter buried under mozzarella sticks, breaded chicken strips, loaded potato skins and onion rings, the pile mounded so high it has slumped past the rim onto the table; molten cheese drapes off one edge in long sagging strands, three ramekins have overflowed and run sauce across the platter into a pool. Setting: a sticky laminate table with a green vinyl booth behind, antique tin signs and lacrosse sticks blurred on the wall, television glow washing over everything. Lighting: dim green-and-amber bar lighting with cold blue television flicker as fill, slightly grimy, nostalgic 1998 casual dining. Camera: overhead flat-lay, 50mm, deep focus, high contrast, faint grease sheen. Square crop, subject centered and filling the frame. Deadpan hyperreal advertising realism. No text, no logos, no packaging labels, no hands, no people.

items.imagePrompt: A careless snapshot taken on an old cheap smartphone by a restaurant employee to upload to a food delivery app. Subject: Nine thick golden-breaded mozzarella sticks packed into a red plastic diner basket on plain checkered paper, one broken open with a long sagging cheese strand stretched between the halves across the basket, a small plastic cup of marinara wedged in the corner and running over. Frontal on-camera flash with no light source visible in frame, a hard blown-out hotspot on the nearest sticks and a hard shadow thrown behind the basket. Shot from too close and slightly above so the basket sits off centre, a stainless prep counter and a stack of lids crowding the background.. EVERYTHING in the frame equally sharp from the food to the back wall - no shallow depth of field, no bokeh, no blurred background, no food styling. Aggressive default smartphone HDR processing: over-sharpened with visible halos along every edge, shadows lifted grey and blotchy, mushy chroma noise, heavy JPEG compression, slightly wrong white balance. The container is off-centre and clipped by one edge of the frame, the camera tilted several degrees off level, shot from too close and slightly above. This is a careless snapshot, NOT a photograph: no artistic composition, no cinematic lighting, no colour grading, no professional food photography, nothing centred or plated. Unstyled, unretouched, honest and a little unappetising - but the food is real food from a real kitchen, generous and identifiable, not a joke about bad food. Square crop.
